=== HANDOFF #10 — epic e369 (Jira Server/Data Center). READ THIS, THEN #9, THEN #8. ===

WORKTREE /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-jira-family. ALWAYS: export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"
NOTE: this session worked on SHORT-LIVED BRANCHES off main rather than one long stack, because the
plan-review gate requires HEAD == the attestation's sha and main moves constantly. That worked far
better than rebasing a stack; keep doing it.

*** THE EPIC'S HEADLINE AC IS PROVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND HAS STAYED PROVEN ACROSS THREE RUNS. ***
`test_a_dc_issue_reaches_the_local_store_inbound` AND
`test_a_local_edit_reaches_the_dc_issue_outbound` both PASS against a real DC instance. Run
30718360110 was 26/26. Run 30721408463 (with 22 new cells added) was 29 passed / 19 failed — and
ALL 26 pre-existing cells still passed there, so nothing regressed.

BOARD: e369 is 22/26 children CLOSED. Remaining: 5200 (J11, in_progress), b586 (in_progress,
waiting only on S2's close), 6a91 (in_progress, change 1191 in review), cc77 (open, NOT started).

CLOSED THIS SESSION: f2f3 (S1), 9f0b, fe15.
MERGED THIS SESSION: 1177, 1179 (S1), 1182 (J11 mutation suite), 1183 (9f0b tests), 1185 (S2),
1186 (fe15). SIX changes.
IN REVIEW: 1188 (J11 fixes), 1190 (S2 number provenance), 1191 (6a91).

--- WHAT EACH REMAINING TICKET NEEDS ---
 * 5200 (J11): land 1188, re-run the harness, then TRIAGE THE FIVE GENUINE FINDINGS listed in the
   "HARNESS RUN 3" comment on that ticket. Do NOT re-derive them; that comment already separates
   13 false reds from 5 real ones.
 * b586: closes as soon as S2 (6758) closes. Nothing else.
 * 6758 (S2): MERGED already. Its close FAILED on ONE criterion — the three researched numbers
   (DC-only / 8.6+ / off-by-default; retry-after + 20% jitter) were stated as fact rather than
   confirmed-or-marked-unverified. Change 1190 fixes exactly that. Land it, then close S2.
 * 6a91: change 1191 in review. Land, then close.
 * cc77: plan now HAS Approach/Scope/Testing (I added them) but is UNREVIEWED and UNIMPLEMENTED.
   It is the biggest remaining piece: annotate ~15-22 `client`/`transport` params as
   `TicketTransport`, then treat every resulting mypy `[attr-defined]` as a finding naming a port
   gap. Do NOT promote `_engine` through the strictness ratchet at the same time — `client: Any`
   satisfies `disallow_untyped_defs` while staying completely blind, which is the whole point of
   the ticket.

--- THE MOST USEFUL THING I LEARNED, AND IT COST TWO WRONG DIAGNOSES ---
**"N failed" is a category, not a cause — and I re-learned it the hard way twice in one run.**
Run 30721408463 reported 19 failures. My first read was "inbound updates are broken". Wrong: 13 of
the 19 were mutations that ROUND-TRIPPED PERFECTLY and tripped only on an idempotence assertion I
had BUNDLED into every cell. My second read, of the outbound cells, was also wrong for the same
reason. Only after categorising all 19 BY WHICH ASSERTION FIRED did the real picture appear.
The structural fix is this epic's own recurring lesson, which I violated while quoting it: an
assertion that can fail for a reason unrelated to the cell's subject BELONGS IN ITS OWN CELL.
Change 1188 hoists idempotence out.

**A TEST FILTER NEARLY BECAME A CATASTROPHIC FALSE ALARM.** The pagination cell reported
"recovered only 0 of 201 seeded issues — 201 silently LOST". That is not data loss. The plan
envelope's `local_id` field is populated from `provenance["local_id"]` and FOR THESE ENTRIES IT
CARRIES THE JIRA KEY — visible in the same run's outbound entries: `{'target': 'RBJISZB-1',
'local_id': 'RBJISZB-1'}`. Matching a derived local id against it matches NOTHING, which is why
the number was a suspiciously round zero rather than a partial. The thin slice's inbound-create
cell already had this right by ORing on `target`. **If a live cell reports total loss, suspect the
filter before the fetch.**

--- STANDING RULES ADDED THIS SESSION (earlier ones in #6-#9 still hold) ---
 * SHORT BRANCHES OFF MAIN, one per ticket. The claim gate compares your HEAD to the attestation's
   verified sha, and main moves every few minutes; `git checkout -B <name> <verified-sha>` then
   claim, then rebase forward. Fighting this with a long stack wastes rounds.
 * `rebar sign-review <id>` re-signs from the recorded review with NO LLM re-run. Use it when a
   review PASSES but signing fails with `store-read-failure` (flock contention from the other
   session) — do not re-run the review.
 * A `Verified -1` is not always your code. Check WHICH JOB failed: this session's -1 on 1188 came
   from the `clear Verified (reset to 0)` infra job exiting 255, with `build-and-test` SKIPPED as a
   consequence — the change was never tested. `recheck` is the remedy. And note the log echoes the
   workflow SCRIPT's own `::error::` lines, which will send you after the wrong cause.
 * VERIFY VENDOR ATTRIBUTES AT RUNTIME, NOT BY NAME. `JIRAError` has BOTH `.headers` and
   `.response.headers`; `.headers` is the REQUEST headers (`self.headers = kwargs.get("headers")`,
   docstring says so), so `Retry-After` is ONLY on `.response.headers`. Reading the obvious one
   would have type-checked and silently never found the header. The S2 test plants a DECOY on the
   wrong attribute so a wrong implementation fails loudly.
 * A MUTATION THAT DOES NOT GO RED IS NOT ALWAYS A WEAK TEST. Two cases this session: (1) the 9f0b
   `setdefault` mutation stayed green because cache-first short-circuits before the buggy line —
   the real defect needs the name already held by a DIFFERENT-PATH module, so the assertion had to
   move to where that state exists; (2) an S2 mutation reported not-caught in a rapid
   mutate/restore batch and WAS caught in isolation with `__pycache__` cleared. Re-check in
   isolation before weakening an assertion.
 * PLAN REVIEWS ARE WORTH THE ROUNDS. Every BLOCK this session named something real: S2 would have
   shipped a rate-limit fix that missed the highest-volume read (`get_comment_map`'s per-issue
   fetch bypasses `_call_logged` entirely); 6a91 would have constructed a value with no receiver;
   and 6a91's reviewer caught that MY claim about 7c26 was false (bindings key on the Jira KEY;
   `record_jira_id` is an additive re-key fallback). Check a disputed finding against the code
   before scoring it wrong — the reviewer was right every time this session.
 * AFTER EDITING A PLAN, GREP THE WHOLE DOCUMENT. Still earning its place: my own sweep caught an
   AC that still carried a justification I had just withdrawn, and three "the ADR" singulars after
   Scope changed to "BOTH ADRs".
